content.comment_body: Hello, I usually work with [version_no] controllers, but now I need to support a customer using [product_name]. The customer wants to: - Send the AI1 value into AM1 if certain conditions are met - Send the AI2 value into AM1 if those conditions are not met I would typically use a 'Move' instruction and enable the input, but I can't determine how to achieve this in [product_name]. Best regards, [user_name]
You can utilize a multiplexer for this. First, can you let us know which [product_name] version you're working with?

[user_name], Thank you for responding so quickly—you're very active here! [article_no] is the [product_name] version the customer and I are using. I began a test in the office. I reached the step where I want to display AM1 on the device’s screen, but I haven’t managed to do it yet. [IMAGE] Best regards, [user_name]

Yes [user_name], that’s true. Please clarify what you want to achieve. Is it just to show a value on the internal [product_name] display? It's not advisable to use arrow buttons for this. Consider presenting several pages on the screen instead. Maybe sketch out what the page layout should be. I've attached a simple example, which is similar to your version.

Hello [user_name], you're right! The use of arrows and displaying on the device screen is just for my bench test. Sorry for the earlier lack of clarity—here’s what I mean: [IMAGE] Best regards, [user_name]

My suggestion is that for simple display purposes, moving to AM1 isn’t necessary. If you actually require the value in AM1, that's a different scenario. The concept you demonstrated is fine and is quite similar to my first sample. You'll need a way to hold the selection bit active, not just edge detection. The more details you share, the more help [user_name] or I can provide.
[user_name], I’m signing off now. I’ll leave you in the capable hands of our [product_name] expert, [user_name]. [user_name], please help out if you can. Many thanks!
Hello, It’s working now—perhaps not the most refined solution. [IMAGE] If anyone has a better idea, feel free to post it. Thanks for all the help, much appreciated! Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user tried to implement a conditional 'move' instruction for analog inputs in a [product_name] system, similar to what they were used to on other [company_name] controllers. They found the process less straightforward due to differences in programming workflow and display options. Forum members recommended using a multiplexer logic, but the user felt the method was more complex than anticipated and struggled with displaying results directly on the device.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expected [product_name] to provide a simple and familiar way to move analog values conditionally and display the result—similar in ease to instructions available on more advanced controller systems.
